_note: Canonical Enqpy test vectors. Every value is emitted directly by the Rev 5.1 reference implementation (84/84 self-test PASS). The Rev 3.0 KATs are unchanged and reproduce byte-for-byte; v5.1 ADDS vectors (Rev 5.1 key domain, both-axes coset, empty plaintext, window boundary, full LOW/MEDIUM profile coverage, the Phase-1 OR_EXP self-referential case, and the NIL key-update policy) and edits none in place. Hex is UPPERCASE with no separators. Enqpy has no associated-data field. A port is Reference-Compatible (CONFORMANCE.md 2.1) when it reproduces every output below exactly.
reference: Enqpy reference implementation Rev 5.1 (Canonical Configuration); 84/84 self-test; the Rev 3.0 KATs are unchanged
spec: FCD Rev 5.1 §13; proof companion [12]. Canonical paper link: https://enqpy.com/technical.html

assertions._comment: Counts the 84 assertions of the C self-test (PDAF + PDAF_SEC + window boundary + NIL key-update). The OWC vector below is a supplementary FCD 13.1 vector; OWC is not exercised by the self-test. As of v5.1 the published groups cover the key-domain, coset, empty-plaintext and window-boundary cases mechanically.

encoding.combine: message combine is byte-wise XOR: CT_byte = W_byte XOR PT_byte, with W_byte = (W_nibble_even << 4) | W_nibble_odd. MOD16 arithmetic is internal to W generation only.

groups.description: One-Way Computation primitive (Nil-Communication Key Update path). Non-overlapping pairs: advance the position pointer by (1+nSkip) per output nibble; output is ~half the input. Matches FCD §13.1. Supplementary vector — not part of the 84-assertion self-test.
PDAF Mode 0 (Dual Key Pointer Add). Internal component; not the primary cipher path. n=10, 30-nibble output.

PDAF Mode 1 (Key Offset Add). The primary key-derivation primitive: a many-to-one MOD16 mixing map. Recovering session keys leaves >= 2 (worst case) / >= 16 (non-degenerate) candidate master keys per compatible OffsetKey, not a unique solution. n=10, 30-nibble output.

Full encrypt/decrypt, Canonical Configuration, all three profiles (n=32 LOW, n=48 MEDIUM, n=64 HIGH). CT length == PT length. For zero plaintext, CT == keystream W. Decryption round-trips to PT; the [+8] coset on either master key, or both, yields identical CT (Theorem 2 equivocation basis). Key domain (Rev 5.1): ek and qk are sampled independently and uniformly with NO ek != qk restriction; an implementation that rejects or resamples equal keys is non-conformant. Profile keys: the HIGH vectors use the canonical values in full; the LOW and MEDIUM vectors use the LAST n nibbles of those same canonical values (a suffix, not a prefix -- see _profile_derivation). Every profile yields a DIFFERENT ciphertext, so these vectors discriminate: an implementation that ignores n and always runs HIGH fails them.

tests._purpose: Rev 5.1 key domain. EK == QK is a permitted sample and MUST be accepted. An implementation that rejects or resamples equal keys is NON-CONFORMANT: rejection sampling punctures the key domain over which Theorems 2 and 3 are proved. Rev 5.0 of the FCD asked for a -1 return here; that requirement is withdrawn.
Zero-length plaintext is legal. Output length equals input length, so the ciphertext is empty and the call returns 0, not -1.

Exercises the 2,048-byte HIGH window and the Phase-5 update that follows it. The full ciphertext is not embedded; check the documented tail bytes, then confirm a 2,050-byte payload round-trips across the boundary.

roundtrip.result: PT recovered across the window boundary

tests._purpose: LOW profile (n=32) keystream isolation. Zero plaintext, so CT == W.
Rev 5.1 key domain at LOW. EK == QK MUST be accepted at every profile.
LOW window is n^2/2 = 512 bytes. Checks the documented tail bytes, then a 514-byte round-trip across the Phase-5 update.

roundtrip.result: PT recovered across the window boundary

tests._purpose: MEDIUM profile (n=48) keystream isolation. Zero plaintext, so CT == W.
Rev 5.1 key domain at MEDIUM. EK == QK MUST be accepted at every profile.
MEDIUM window is n^2/2 = 1152 bytes. Checks the documented tail bytes, then a 1154-byte round-trip across the Phase-5 update.

roundtrip.result: PT recovered across the window boundary

groups.description: PDAF Mode 1 applied to itself (VK = OK) — the Phase-1 OR_EXP expansion of FCD §13.2a. PDAF_SEC computes OR_EXP = PDAF1(or_ctr_nibs, or_ctr_nibs) at the profile n, where or_ctr_nibs is the 64-bit counter as 16 nibbles, most significant first, zero-padded to n. Reachable through the public PDAF() entry point by passing the same array as both ValueKey and OffsetKey. Note that small counters give low-entropy OR_EXP: that is expected and correct — OR_EXP contributes counter state and diffusion, NOT uniqueness. Nonce freshness is probabilistic and comes from the CSPRNG OR component (FCD §7.2).

tests._purpose: or_ctr = 0xA5C3 — a non-trivial value showing the propagation behaviour

groups.description: Nil-Communication credential rotation policy, ENQPY_NIL_COMM_UPDATE. Method 2 (external entropy) is REQUIRED; Method 1 (deterministic chain) is PROHIBITED because it is SIMULABLE — the chain is a public function of the current key state, so an adversary holding that state computes the next one and the rotation resets nothing. A conforming implementation MUST reject Method 1 and MUST reject Method 2 called without external entropy. Note that coset behaviour is not the discriminator: Method 2 also maps the four-element [+8] coset to a single new pair.

tests._purpose: Method 1 is prohibited and MUST be rejected.
Method 2 with external entropy succeeds and produces the new credential pair.
tests.coset_maps_to_single_pair: yes — (EK+8, QK+8) yields the same ek_new/qk_new

tests._purpose: Method 2 without external entropy MUST be rejected — the external entropy is the whole point of the method.

_profile_derivation: LOW (n=32) and MEDIUM (n=48) key material is the LAST n nibbles of the canonical HIGH ek/qk/or. A suffix is used deliberately. With a PREFIX the first 16 keystream nibbles are identical at every profile -- at c=0 no index exceeds p+15+1 = 31 < n, and with or_ctr=1 the counter expansion agrees over that range -- so a prefix-derived zero-plaintext vector would be reproduced by an implementation that ignored n entirely. The suffix makes the three profiles disagree, which is what a conformance vector has to do.
